title.zh: 「第一次」是带收据的篝火故事

summary.en: Who invented metal? Who invented punk? Historians fight. Landmarks just give you a door that opens into the fight.
summary.zh: 谁发明了金属？谁发明了朋克？史家会吵。Landmark 只给你一扇能走进那场架的门。

body.en:
Ask a metalhead who started metal and watch the evening become a contact sport. Sabbath's rain-soaked tritone? Earlier underground noise? Some blues player who bent a note until it hurt? Everyone has a holy relic.

That's fine. Rock "firsts" are rarely clean patents. They're moments when a sound becomes undeniable in public—when enough people hear it that later bands have to react.

On band pages, the Landmark card is our way of saying: start here. Not "this is the only truth," but "this track is a good hinge—year, gut-punch, and the genres it shoved open." On genre pages, pioneer acts are the relatives who brought the weird casserole that somehow became tradition.

We keep landmarks fused to stories on purpose. A separate "museum of firsts" turns into a ranking fight before lunch. Next to Why it matters, a debut track becomes a scene you can walk into.

Argue later if you want. First, press play on something that rearranges the furniture in your chest. Then follow who answered.
body.zh:
问一个金属听众谁开创了金属，然后看着夜晚变成接触性运动。Sabbath 雨里的三全音？更早的地下噪音？某个把音弯到疼的 Blues 琴手？人人都有圣物。

没关系。摇滚的「第一次」很少像干净专利。它们是声音在公众面前变得无法忽视的瞬间——够多人听见了，后面的乐队就不得不反应。

乐队页上的 Landmark 卡片，意思是：从这儿进门。不是「唯一真理」，而是「这首是好枢纽——年份、胸口一击、以及它撞开的流派」。流派页上的开创乐队，则是带来那锅奇怪焗菜、结果变成传统的亲戚。

我们故意把 landmark 融在故事旁边。单独开一座「第一次博物馆」，午饭前就会变成排行架。贴着「为何重要」，一首首曲会变成你能走进去的现场。

想吵可以稍后吵。先按播放，找那种把胸口家具重新摆过的东西。然后看谁回答了它。
